48:const IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES: ReadonlySet<TenantLifecycleStatus> = new Set(["DELETING", "QUIESCING", "PURGING"]);
49:
50:export interface CloseOrganizationResult {
51:  tenantId: string;
52:  status: TenantLifecycleStatus;
53:  /** False when the record was already DELETING+ and this call only repeated the launch. */
54:  transitioned: boolean;
55:}
56:
57:export class CloseOrganizationService {
58:  constructor(
59:    private readonly store: SystemMutationStore,
60:    private readonly reader: TenantLifecycleReader,
61:    private readonly executions: TenantPurgeExecutionStarter,
62:    private readonly tableName: string,
63:    private readonly now: () => string = () => new Date().toISOString(),
64:  ) {}
65:
66:  async close(ctx: RequestContext): Promise<CloseOrganizationResult> {
67:    const tenantId = ctx.tenant.tenantId;
68:    authorize({ context: ctx, action: "organization:close", resource: { tenantId } });
69:
70:    const record = await this.reader.read(tenantId);
71:    if (!record) {
72:      throw new NotFoundError("Organization lifecycle record not found.", { organizationId: tenantId });
73:    }
74:    if (CLOSURE_UNAVAILABLE_STATUSES.has(record.status)) {
75:      throw new OrganizationClosureUnavailableError(undefined, { organizationId: tenantId, status: record.status });
76:    }
77:
78:    let transitioned = false;
79:    if (record.status === "ACTIVE") {
80:      try {
81:        await transitionTenantLifecycle({
82:          store: this.store,
83:          tableName: this.tableName,
84:          tenantId,
85:          from: "ACTIVE",
86:          to: "DELETING",
87:          expectedVersion: record.version,
88:          now: this.now,
89:        });
90:        transitioned = true;
91:      } catch (err) {
92:        if (!(err instanceof SystemMutationConflictError)) throw err;
93:        // A concurrent close() (double-click, retried request) won the race. Re-read once: if the
94:        // record legitimately landed on an in-flight state, this call simply joins that closure
95:        // and proceeds to the shared idempotent launch below. Anything else Ã¢â‚¬â€ still ACTIVE, or
96:        // raced into a stuck state Ã¢â‚¬â€ is genuinely unexpected and is not papered over.
97:        const after = await this.reader.read(tenantId);
98:        if (!after || !IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES.has(after.status)) throw err;
99:      }
100:    } else if (!IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES.has(record.status)) {
101:      // Exhaustiveness guard: ACTIVE, the 4 unavailable states, and the 3 in-flight states cover
102:      // every TenantLifecycleStatus. Reaching here means a status was added without deciding what
103:      // closing should do with it Ã¢â‚¬â€ fail loudly rather than silently launching an execution.
104:      throw new OrganizationClosureUnavailableError(undefined, { organizationId: tenantId, status: record.status });
105:    }
106:
107:    await this.executions.startExecution({ name: tenantId, input: { tenantId } });
108:
109:    return { tenantId, status: transitioned ? "DELETING" : record.status, transitioned };
110:  }
111:}
1:/**
2: * TenantLifecycleRecord Ã¢â‚¬â€ W3-07 tenant deletion fence (D-067, `docs/architecture/decisions-log.md`;
3: * design approved via Claude<->Codex protocol, 9.2/9.1, `docs/architecture/reviews/
4: * w3-07-tenant-fence-round3-active-only-design/claude-analysis-active-only-fence.md` Ã‚Â§G/Ã‚Â§H).
5: *
6: * A tombstone item that outlives the tenant's own data cascade Ã¢â‚¬â€ same pattern as
7: * `IdentityMapping` (identity-mapping-repository.ts): it lives outside the normal purge
8: * cascade permanently, because it is the one artifact that must survive to prove "this
9: * tenant existed and was deleted" and to block first-login from silently reprovisioning a
10: * deleted tenant (the root cause the design doc traces D-063's failure to).
11: *
12: * Lives under `src/shared/` (not `src/modules/identity/domain/`) deliberately: it is
13: * consumed by `src/shared/tenant-lifecycle/tenant-business-mutation.ts`, a shared/
14: * infrastructure-level fencing primitive every tenant-scoped business mutation across
15: * modules will eventually route through Ã¢â‚¬â€ and `shared/**` must never import from
16: * `modules/**` (`.dependency-cruiser.cjs`'s `shared-must-not-reach-modules` rule). Placing
17: * the record's own domain type here, instead of in `identity/domain` with the lane
18: * importing it back out, keeps the dependency direction modules -> shared intact.
19: */
20:import type { EntityKey } from "../dynamodb/occ.js";
21:
22:/**
23: * Forward-only state machine (approved design Ã‚Â§G):
24: *   ACTIVE -> DELETING -> QUIESCING -> PURGING -> VERIFIED -> DELETED
25: * Any of DELETING/QUIESCING/PURGING/VERIFIED can additionally move to BLOCKED/HELD (stuck
26: * state Ã¢â‚¬â€ legal hold or a purge error that keeps failing) and back to the SAME state once
27: * remediated. ACTIVE is never re-entered from any other state (no "un-delete") and DELETED
28: * is a true terminal Ã¢â‚¬â€ nothing transitions out of it (the sweeper described in the design
29: * doc repairs residue in place, it never re-opens the lifecycle record's status).
30: */
31:export type TenantLifecycleStatus =
32:  | "ACTIVE"
33:  | "DELETING"
34:  | "QUIESCING"
35:  | "PURGING"
36:  | "VERIFIED"
37:  | "DELETED"
38:  | "BLOCKED"
39:  | "HELD";
40:
41:export interface TenantLifecycleRecord extends EntityKey {
42:  SK: "LIFECYCLE";
43:  entityType: "TenantLifecycleRecord";
44:  tenantId: string;
45:  status: TenantLifecycleStatus;
46:  /** Set when entering BLOCKED/HELD and cleared on remediation back to the prior state Ã¢â‚¬â€ a
47:   * short machine-readable reason for the stuck state (e.g. "PURGE_S3_ERRORS",
48:   * "LEGAL_HOLD"), never free text containing tenant PII. */
49:  blockedReason?: string;
50:  /** The state BLOCKED/HELD was entered from, so remediation knows where to resume Ã¢â‚¬â€
51:   * required whenever status is BLOCKED/HELD, absent otherwise. */
52:  blockedFrom?: TenantLifecycleStatus;
53:  createdAt: string;
54:  updatedAt: string;
55:  version: number;
56:}
57:
58:export function tenantLifecycleKey(tenantId: string): EntityKey {
59:  return { PK: `TENANT#${tenantId}#LIFECYCLE`, SK: "LIFECYCLE" };
60:}
61:
62:/**
63: * Statuses under which a `TenantBusinessMutation` may be admitted Ã¢â‚¬â€ deliberately just
64: * `ACTIVE` (approved design Ã‚Â§H invariant 1: "Nenhuma mutaÃƒÂ§ÃƒÂ£o de negÃƒÂ³cio tenant-scoped
65: * commita em DynamoDB sem ConditionCheck de TenantLifecycleRecord.status = ACTIVE").
66: */
67:export const TENANT_ACTIVE_STATUS: TenantLifecycleStatus = "ACTIVE";
68:
69:/** Forward-only transition graph. A state maps to the set of states it may legally move to
70: * next; BLOCKED/HELD's own allowed targets depend on `blockedFrom` (checked separately by
71: * `canResumeFromBlocked`, since the graph itself can't express "return to wherever you came
72: * from" as a fixed edge list). */
73:const FORWARD_TRANSITIONS: Record<TenantLifecycleStatus, ReadonlySet<TenantLifecycleStatus>> = {
74:  ACTIVE: new Set(["DELETING"]),
75:  DELETING: new Set(["QUIESCING", "BLOCKED", "HELD"]),
76:  QUIESCING: new Set(["PURGING", "BLOCKED", "HELD"]),
77:  PURGING: new Set(["VERIFIED", "BLOCKED", "HELD"]),
78:  VERIFIED: new Set(["DELETED", "BLOCKED", "HELD"]),
79:  DELETED: new Set([]),
80:  BLOCKED: new Set([]), // only canResumeFromBlocked() below, not a fixed forward edge
81:  HELD: new Set([]),
82:};
83:
84:/**
85: * True if `from -> to` is a legal forward transition, OR a remediation resume out of
86: * BLOCKED/HELD back to the exact state it was blocked from. Never true for anything that
87: * would re-enter ACTIVE or leave DELETED Ã¢â‚¬â€ those two guarantees are the entire point of
88: * this fence (approved design Ã‚Â§H invariant 4, Ã‚Â§Q "no ACTIVE reversion, no DELETED
89: * resurrection").
90: */
91:export function canTransition(from: TenantLifecycleStatus, to: TenantLifecycleStatus, blockedFrom?: TenantLifecycleStatus): boolean {
92:  if (to === "ACTIVE") return false; // never re-enter ACTIVE from anywhere
93:  if (from === "DELETED") return false; // DELETED is terminal, nothing leaves it
94:  if ((from === "BLOCKED" || from === "HELD") && blockedFrom) {
95:    return to === blockedFrom;
96:  }
97:  return FORWARD_TRANSITIONS[from]?.has(to) ?? false;
98:}
99:
100:export class InvalidTenantLifecycleTransitionError extends Error {
101:  constructor(
102:    public readonly from: TenantLifecycleStatus,
103:    public readonly to: TenantLifecycleStatus,
104:  ) {
105:    super(`Invalid TenantLifecycleRecord transition: ${from} -> ${to}`);
106:    this.name = "InvalidTenantLifecycleTransitionError";
107:  }
108:}
109:
110:/** Throws InvalidTenantLifecycleTransitionError instead of returning false Ã¢â‚¬â€ for callers
111: * (e.g. the future lifecycle-transition worker) that want a fail-fast assertion rather than
112: * a boolean they must remember to check. */
113:export function assertValidTransition(from: TenantLifecycleStatus, to: TenantLifecycleStatus, blockedFrom?: TenantLifecycleStatus): void {
114:  if (!canTransition(from, to, blockedFrom)) {
115:    throw new InvalidTenantLifecycleTransitionError(from, to);
116:  }
117:}

178:export type AuthorizationDenialReason = "TENANT_MISMATCH" | "NO_MEMBERSHIP" | "INSUFFICIENT_ROLE" | "RESOURCE_OWNERSHIP_MISMATCH";
179:
180:export class AuthorizationDeniedError extends Error {
181:  constructor(
182:    readonly reason: AuthorizationDenialReason,
183:    readonly action: Action,
184:  ) {
185:    super(`Authorization denied for action "${action}": ${reason}`);
186:    this.name = "AuthorizationDeniedError";
187:  }
188:}
189:
190:/**
191: * authorize() Ã¢â‚¬â€ implementation-blueprint.md Ã‚Â§4.3: "authorize() verifica primeiro
192: * igualdade de tenant, depois papel e vÃƒÂ­nculo por recurso." Throws
193: * AuthorizationDeniedError (never returns false) so callers cannot forget to check
194: * a boolean result Ã¢â‚¬â€ the http layer maps this to AuthorizationError (403).
195: *
196: * Order matters and is deliberately fail-closed at every step:
197: *  1. context must carry at least one role (no membership => no access at all).
198: *  2. if a resource is supplied, resource.tenantId MUST equal context.tenant.tenantId Ã¢â‚¬â€
199: *     this is the check that makes cross-tenant ID substitution fail, independent of
200: *     role, and independent of what the caller *claims* the resource's tenant is (the
201: *     resource object here must always be populated from a DB read keyed by the
202: *     authenticated tenantId, never from client input Ã¢â‚¬â€ see repository contract).
203: *  3. role must be sufficient for the action.
204: *  4. if the resource declares an owner/assignee, membership role alone isn't enough
205: *     for actions that are resource-scoped by ownership in the future; MVP has no
206: *     per-item ownership finer than tenant, so this step is a no-op today but kept
207: *     explicit so a future item-level ACL doesn't require re-deriving this function.
208: */
209:export function authorize(input: AuthorizationInput): void {
210:  const { context, action, resource } = input;
211:  const roles = context.tenant.roles as Role[];
212:
213:  if (roles.length === 0) {
214:    throw new AuthorizationDeniedError("NO_MEMBERSHIP", action);
215:  }
216:
217:  if (resource && resource.tenantId !== context.tenant.tenantId) {
218:    throw new AuthorizationDeniedError("TENANT_MISMATCH", action);
219:  }
220:
221:  const allowedRoles = ACTION_ROLES[action];
222:  const hasRole = roles.some((role) => allowedRoles.has(role));
223:  if (!hasRole) {
224:    throw new AuthorizationDeniedError("INSUFFICIENT_ROLE", action);
225:  }
226:
227:  if (resource?.assigneeUserId && resource.ownerUserId) {
228:    const isOwnerOrAssignee =
229:      resource.ownerUserId === context.principal.userId ||
230:      resource.assigneeUserId === context.principal.userId;
231:    // OWNER and ADMIN bypass per-resource ownership (tenant-wide content admin, B2B-7 -
232:    // ADMIN has parity with OWNER over business resources, see authorization.ts role model
233:    // comment above), MEMBER/VIEWER scoped resources require ownership match once per-item
234:    // ACLs exist. This is enforced only when both fields ARE present (defensive for future
235:    // use), never invented from nothing.
236:    if (!roles.includes("OWNER") && !roles.includes("ADMIN") && !isOwnerOrAssignee) {
237:      throw new AuthorizationDeniedError("RESOURCE_OWNERSHIP_MISMATCH", action);
238:    }
239:  }
240:}
1:/**

3: * Ã‚Â§11. Steps:
4: *  1. validation already performed by the API Gateway authorizer (JWT signature/exp) Ã¢â‚¬â€ this
5: *     function receives already-validated claims, it does not verify JWT signatures;
6: *  2. bootstrap the global identity (`IdentityBootstrapService`, 2-item atomic create) Ã¢â‚¬â€

9: *     `HAS_USABLE_MEMBERSHIP` proceeds to a working `RequestContext`, everything else throws

41:export interface ResolveRequestContextInput {
42:  claims: ValidatedClaims;
43:  requestId: string;
44:  correlationId: string;
45:  /** From `X-Organization-Id` (BFF-derived, Wave B2B-6/D-101) Ã¢â‚¬â€ REQUIRED (not `?:`), even
46:   * though `undefined` is a valid value, so the compiler blocks every real call site (56 across

56:export class RequestContextResolver {
57:  private readonly bootstrap: IdentityBootstrapService;
58:  private readonly onboarding: OnboardingStateResolver;
59:
60:  constructor(
61:    private readonly users: UserRepository,
62:    private readonly globalUsers: GlobalUserRepository,
63:    private readonly organizations: OrganizationStore,
64:    private readonly ids: IdGenerator,
65:    store: IdentityStore,
66:    tableName: string,
67:  ) {
68:    this.bootstrap = new IdentityBootstrapService(store, tableName);
69:    this.onboarding = new OnboardingStateResolver(organizations);
70:  }
71:
72:  async resolve(input: ResolveRequestContextInput): Promise<RequestContext> {
73:    const { claims } = input;
74:
75:    const newUserId = this.ids.newUserId();
76:    const { user } = await this.bootstrap.bootstrapUser(claims.sub, newUserId);
77:
78:    if (user.identityStatus !== "ACTIVE") {
79:      throw new AuthenticationError("User is not active.", { userId: user.userId });
80:    }
81:
82:    // Step 5 (user-global watermark, Ã‚Â§10 Ã¢â‚¬â€ was UserProfile.globalLogoutAfter pre-cutover).
83:    if (user.globalLogoutAfter && claims.issuedAt < user.globalLogoutAfter) {
84:      throw new AuthenticationError("Session revoked (global logout).", { userId: user.userId });
85:    }
86:
87:    let deviceSession;
88:    if (claims.deviceId) {
89:      deviceSession = await this.globalUsers.getDeviceSession(user.userId, claims.deviceId);
90:      if (deviceSession) {
91:        if (deviceSession.status === "REVOKED") {
92:          throw new AuthenticationError("Session revoked (device logout).", { deviceId: claims.deviceId });
93:        }
94:        if (deviceSession.deviceLogoutAfter && claims.issuedAt < deviceSession.deviceLogoutAfter) {
95:          throw new AuthenticationError("Session revoked (device logout).", { deviceId: claims.deviceId });
96:        }
97:      }
98:    }
99:    const sessionId = deviceSession?.sessionId ?? this.ids.newSessionId();
100:
101:    const onboardingState = await this.onboarding.resolve(user.userId);
102:    if (onboardingState !== "HAS_USABLE_MEMBERSHIP") {
103:      throw new OnboardingRequiredError(onboardingState, { userId: user.userId });
104:    }
105:
106:    const membership = await this.resolveActiveMembership(user.userId, input.organizationIdHint);
107:
108:    const roles = this.resolveRoles(membership.role);
109:
110:    // ProfileService's invariant ("a UserProfile is guaranteed to already exist by the time any
111:    // RequestContext resolves") must keep holding post-cutover, now per-Organization instead of
112:    // per-legacy-tenant Ã¢â‚¬â€ provisioned lazily here, the first time this (organizationId, userId)
113:    // pair resolves, instead of at bootstrap time (no Organization is known yet at bootstrap).
114:    await this.users.createProfileIfAbsent({
115:      tenantId: membership.organizationId,
116:      userId: user.userId,
117:      identitySubject: claims.sub,
118:      emailNormalized: user.emailNormalized,
119:      roles,
120:      status: "ACTIVE",
121:    });
122:
123:    return {
124:      requestId: input.requestId,
125:      correlationId: input.correlationId,
126:      principal: {
127:        userId: user.userId,
128:        cognitoSubject: claims.sub,
129:        sessionId,
130:        deviceId: claims.deviceId,
131:      },
132:      tenant: {
133:        tenantId: membership.organizationId,
134:        membershipId: membership.membershipId,
135:        roles,
136:      },
137:      auth: {
138:        issuedAt: claims.issuedAt,
139:        expiresAt: claims.expiresAt,
140:        tokenId: claims.tokenId,
141:      },
142:    };
143:  }
144:
145:  /**
146:   * Physical model Ã‚Â§11's resolution chain: `... -> BFF session.activeOrganizationId (seleÃƒÂ§ÃƒÂ£o)
147:   * -> GetItem direto Membership(userId, organizationId) -> TenantLifecycleRecord ACTIVE ->
148:   * RequestContext`. Wave B2B-6 (D-101) closes the transport gap D-095 left open (achado 2.1) -
149:   * `organizationIdHint` (from `X-Organization-Id`, BFF-derived, never client-controlled) is
150:   * revalidated via `resolveWorkingOrganization()` (consolidates Membership ACTIVE + lifecycle
151:   * ACTIVE - replaces the separate `AuthenticationError` this function used to throw for the
152:   * lifecycle half of that check). Hint absent falls back to deriving via GSI4: exactly one
153:   * ACTIVE Membership (today's common case, unchanged behavior) or a named, non-crashing error
154:   * for 0/>1 - no writer produced a 2nd ACTIVE Membership for the same user before Wave B2B-8
155:   * made it reachable, per D-095/D-096's own registered deviation.
156:   */
157:  private async resolveActiveMembership(userId: string, organizationIdHint: string | undefined): Promise<Membership> {
158:    if (organizationIdHint) {
159:      const result = await resolveWorkingOrganization(this.organizations, userId, organizationIdHint);
160:      if (result.status === "UNAVAILABLE") {
161:        throw new OrganizationUnavailableError("This organization is not available in your current context.", { organizationId: organizationIdHint });
162:      }
163:      return result.membership;
164:    }
165:
166:    const active = await resolveActiveMemberships(this.organizations, userId);
167:    if (active.length === 0) {
168:      throw new InternalError("OnboardingStateResolver reported HAS_USABLE_MEMBERSHIP but no ACTIVE Membership was found on re-resolution.", { userId });
169:    }
170:    if (active.length > 1) {
171:      throw new OrganizationSelectionRequiredError("Multiple organizations are available; select one via X-Organization-Id.", { userId, activeCount: active.length });
172:    }
173:    const [membership] = active;
174:    if (!membership) {
175:      throw new InternalError("Unreachable: active.length === 1 but active[0] is undefined.", { userId });
176:    }
177:    // Sem hint, a ÃƒÂºnica Membership ACTIVE ainda precisa da mesma checagem de lifecycle - nunca
178:    // um atalho que confie na hidrataÃƒÂ§ÃƒÂ£o de resolveActiveMemberships() sozinha (essa funÃƒÂ§ÃƒÂ£o sÃƒÂ³
179:    // checa Membership.status, nÃƒÂ£o TenantLifecycleRecord).
180:    const result = await resolveWorkingOrganization(this.organizations, userId, membership.organizationId);
181:    if (result.status === "UNAVAILABLE") {
182:      throw new OrganizationUnavailableError("This organization is not available in your current context.", { organizationId: membership.organizationId });
183:    }
184:    return result.membership;
185:  }
186:
187:  /** B2B-7 (D-097/D-098) closed the gap named in D-095: `authorization.ts` now recognizes all
188:   * 4 real `Membership.role` values. The assert stays (fail-closed, Codex Rodada 1 achado
189:   * 2.2/Rodada 2 mudanÃƒÂ§a F, D-095) for any value outside that domain Ã¢â‚¬â€ loud, not silent,
190:   * instead of letting an unrecognized role fail every `authorize()` check via that matrix's
191:   * own unsafe cast. */
192:  private resolveRoles(role: Membership["role"]): string[] {
193:    if (role !== "OWNER" && role !== "ADMIN" && role !== "MEMBER" && role !== "VIEWER") {
194:      throw new UnsupportedMembershipRoleError(role);
195:    }
196:    return [role];
197:  }
198:}

55:function toResponse(appError: AppError): HttpResponse {
56:  const status = STATUS_BY_CATEGORY[appError.category] ?? 500;
57:  return { statusCode: status, body: appError.toJSON() };
58:}
59:
60:async function withErrorMapping(fn: () => Promise<HttpResponse>): Promise<HttpResponse> {
61:  try {
62:    return await fn();
63:  } catch (err) {
64:    if (err instanceof AuthorizationDeniedError) {
65:      auditAuthorizationDenied({ reason: err.reason, action: err.action });
66:      return toResponse(new AuthorizationError(err.message, { reason: err.reason }));
67:    }
68:    const appError = err instanceof AppError ? err : toAppError(err);
69:    return toResponse(appError);
70:  }
71:}

73:export async function handleCloseOrganization(deps: OrganizationLifecycleHttpDeps, req: HttpRequest<CloseOrganizationRequest>): Promise<HttpResponse> {
74:  return withErrorMapping(async () => {
75:    const context = await deps.resolver.resolve({ claims: req.claims, requestId: req.requestId, correlationId: req.correlationId, organizationIdHint: req.headers?.["x-organization-id"] });
76:
77:    // Compared against the RESOLVED tenantId, never against anything else the client sent - the
78:    // confirmation proves intent about the organization the caller is actually authenticated
79:    // into, so a stale browser tab pointed at a different org cannot close this one.
80:    if (req.body?.confirmOrganizationId !== context.tenant.tenantId) {
81:      throw new ValidationError("confirmOrganizationId must match the current organization id to confirm closure.");
82:    }
83:
84:    const result = await deps.closeOrganization.close(context);
85:    return { statusCode: 202, body: { organizationId: result.tenantId, status: result.status } };
86:  });

/**
 * TenantLifecycleRecord Ã¢â‚¬â€ W3-07 tenant deletion fence (D-067, `docs/architecture/decisions-log.md`;
 * design approved via Claude<->Codex protocol, 9.2/9.1, `docs/architecture/reviews/
 * w3-07-tenant-fence-round3-active-only-design/claude-analysis-active-only-fence.md` Ã‚Â§G/Ã‚Â§H).
 *
 * A tombstone item that outlives the tenant's own data cascade Ã¢â‚¬â€ same pattern as
 * `IdentityMapping` (identity-mapping-repository.ts): it lives outside the normal purge
 * cascade permanently, because it is the one artifact that must survive to prove "this
 * tenant existed and was deleted" and to block first-login from silently reprovisioning a
 * deleted tenant (the root cause the design doc traces D-063's failure to).
 *
 * Lives under `src/shared/` (not `src/modules/identity/domain/`) deliberately: it is
 * consumed by `src/shared/tenant-lifecycle/tenant-business-mutation.ts`, a shared/
 * infrastructure-level fencing primitive every tenant-scoped business mutation across
 * modules will eventually route through Ã¢â‚¬â€ and `shared/**` must never import from
 * `modules/**` (`.dependency-cruiser.cjs`'s `shared-must-not-reach-modules` rule). Placing
 * the record's own domain type here, instead of in `identity/domain` with the lane
 * importing it back out, keeps the dependency direction modules -> shared intact.
 */
import type { EntityKey } from "../dynamodb/occ.js";

/**
 * Forward-only state machine (approved design Ã‚Â§G):
 *   ACTIVE -> DELETING -> QUIESCING -> PURGING -> VERIFIED -> DELETED
 * Any of DELETING/QUIESCING/PURGING/VERIFIED can additionally move to BLOCKED/HELD (stuck
 * state Ã¢â‚¬â€ legal hold or a purge error that keeps failing) and back to the SAME state once
 * remediated. ACTIVE is never re-entered from any other state (no "un-delete") and DELETED
 * is a true terminal Ã¢â‚¬â€ nothing transitions out of it (the sweeper described in the design
 * doc repairs residue in place, it never re-opens the lifecycle record's status).
 */
export type TenantLifecycleStatus =
  | "ACTIVE"
  | "DELETING"
  | "QUIESCING"
  | "PURGING"
  | "VERIFIED"
  | "DELETED"
  | "BLOCKED"
  | "HELD";

export interface TenantLifecycleRecord extends EntityKey {
  SK: "LIFECYCLE";
  entityType: "TenantLifecycleRecord";
  tenantId: string;
  status: TenantLifecycleStatus;
  /** Set when entering BLOCKED/HELD and cleared on remediation back to the prior state Ã¢â‚¬â€ a
   * short machine-readable reason for the stuck state (e.g. "PURGE_S3_ERRORS",
   * "LEGAL_HOLD"), never free text containing tenant PII. */
  blockedReason?: string;
  /** The state BLOCKED/HELD was entered from, so remediation knows where to resume Ã¢â‚¬â€
   * required whenever status is BLOCKED/HELD, absent otherwise. */
  blockedFrom?: TenantLifecycleStatus;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
  version: number;
}

export function tenantLifecycleKey(tenantId: string): EntityKey {
  return { PK: `TENANT#${tenantId}#LIFECYCLE`, SK: "LIFECYCLE" };
}

/**
 * Statuses under which a `TenantBusinessMutation` may be admitted Ã¢â‚¬â€ deliberately just
 * `ACTIVE` (approved design Ã‚Â§H invariant 1: "Nenhuma mutaÃƒÂ§ÃƒÂ£o de negÃƒÂ³cio tenant-scoped
 * commita em DynamoDB sem ConditionCheck de TenantLifecycleRecord.status = ACTIVE").
 */
export const TENANT_ACTIVE_STATUS: TenantLifecycleStatus = "ACTIVE";

/** Forward-only transition graph. A state maps to the set of states it may legally move to
 * next; BLOCKED/HELD's own allowed targets depend on `blockedFrom` (checked separately by
 * `canResumeFromBlocked`, since the graph itself can't express "return to wherever you came
 * from" as a fixed edge list). */
const FORWARD_TRANSITIONS: Record<TenantLifecycleStatus, ReadonlySet<TenantLifecycleStatus>> = {
  ACTIVE: new Set(["DELETING"]),
  DELETING: new Set(["QUIESCING", "BLOCKED", "HELD"]),
  QUIESCING: new Set(["PURGING", "BLOCKED", "HELD"]),
  PURGING: new Set(["VERIFIED", "BLOCKED", "HELD"]),
  VERIFIED: new Set(["DELETED", "BLOCKED", "HELD"]),
  DELETED: new Set([]),
  BLOCKED: new Set([]), // only canResumeFromBlocked() below, not a fixed forward edge
  HELD: new Set([]),
};

/**
 * True if `from -> to` is a legal forward transition, OR a remediation resume out of
 * BLOCKED/HELD back to the exact state it was blocked from. Never true for anything that
 * would re-enter ACTIVE or leave DELETED Ã¢â‚¬â€ those two guarantees are the entire point of
 * this fence (approved design Ã‚Â§H invariant 4, Ã‚Â§Q "no ACTIVE reversion, no DELETED
 * resurrection").
 */
export function canTransition(from: TenantLifecycleStatus, to: TenantLifecycleStatus, blockedFrom?: TenantLifecycleStatus): boolean {
  if (to === "ACTIVE") return false; // never re-enter ACTIVE from anywhere
  if (from === "DELETED") return false; // DELETED is terminal, nothing leaves it
  if ((from === "BLOCKED" || from === "HELD") && blockedFrom) {
    return to === blockedFrom;
  }
  return FORWARD_TRANSITIONS[from]?.has(to) ?? false;
}

export class InvalidTenantLifecycleTransitionError extends Error {
  constructor(
    public readonly from: TenantLifecycleStatus,
    public readonly to: TenantLifecycleStatus,
  ) {
    super(`Invalid TenantLifecycleRecord transition: ${from} -> ${to}`);
    this.name = "InvalidTenantLifecycleTransitionError";
  }
}

/** Throws InvalidTenantLifecycleTransitionError instead of returning false Ã¢â‚¬â€ for callers
 * (e.g. the future lifecycle-transition worker) that want a fail-fast assertion rather than
 * a boolean they must remember to check. */
export function assertValidTransition(from: TenantLifecycleStatus, to: TenantLifecycleStatus, blockedFrom?: TenantLifecycleStatus): void {
  if (!canTransition(from, to, blockedFrom)) {
    throw new InvalidTenantLifecycleTransitionError(from, to);
  }
}

/**
 * CloseOrganizationService Ã¢â‚¬â€ W3-07 purge orchestrator (D-124, implementing D-121's approved
 * design, Rodada 2 Fix 1 with Rodada 3 Fix 8's corrected step ordering).
 *
 * The single real trigger surface for tenant deletion: moves the tenant's `TenantLifecycleRecord`
 * `ACTIVE -> DELETING` and launches the tenant-purge Step Functions execution that drives every
 * remaining transition. Before this service existed, both `transitionTenantLifecycle` and
 * `purgeTenant()` were real, working, and completely unreachable Ã¢â‚¬â€ nothing in production ever
 * called either.
 *
 * Step ordering is load-bearing and was corrected during the design protocol (Rodada 3 Fix 8): the
 * terminal-state check runs BEFORE the unconditional `StartExecution`, not after. Rodada 2's
 * original wording implied any post-`ACTIVE` status should trigger a fresh launch, which would
 * have re-launched executions for VERIFIED/DELETED/BLOCKED/HELD tenants Ã¢â‚¬â€ states where a purge
 * execution is either finished or deliberately parked awaiting an operator.
 *
 * `StartExecution` IS called unconditionally for the genuinely in-flight states
 * (`DELETING`/`QUIESCING`/`PURGING`), including when this call performed no write at all. That is
 * the established `start-extraction-run.ts` idiom, not an oversight: gating the launch on "did I
 * just write the record" orphans the tenant forever whenever the DynamoDB transition commits but
 * the subsequent `StartExecution` fails transiently Ã¢â‚¬â€ the record would sit in DELETING with no
 * execution behind it, and every retry would skip the launch because the write already happened.
 * Step Functions' own name-based uniqueness (`name: tenantId`) is what makes calling it every
 * time safe.
 */
import { authorize } from "../../identity/domain/authorization.js";
import type { RequestContext } from "../../identity/domain/request-context.js";
import { OrganizationClosureUnavailableError, NotFoundError } from "../../../shared/errors/app-error.js";
import { SystemMutationConflictError, transitionTenantLifecycle, type SystemMutationStore } from "../../../shared/tenant-lifecycle/system-mutation.js";
import type { TenantLifecycleRecord, TenantLifecycleStatus } from "../../../shared/tenant-lifecycle/tenant-lifecycle-record.js";
import type { TenantPurgeExecutionStarter } from "../../../shared/tenant-lifecycle/tenant-purge-execution-starter.js";

/** Same narrow read contract the orchestrator's transition handler uses Ã¢â‚¬â€ `ConsistentRead: true`
 * is mandatory, since this read produces the `expectedVersion` the OCC-fenced transition below is
 * conditioned on. */
export interface TenantLifecycleReader {
  read(tenantId: string): Promise<TenantLifecycleRecord | undefined>;
}

/** States where a purge is either already finished or parked awaiting a human Ã¢â‚¬â€ closing is
 * refused outright rather than re-launched. Named "unavailable", not "terminal": an operator can
 * still remediate BLOCKED/HELD (`tenant-lifecycle-record.ts`), so these are not all true terminal
 * states. */
const CLOSURE_UNAVAILABLE_STATUSES: ReadonlySet<TenantLifecycleStatus> = new Set(["VERIFIED", "DELETED", "BLOCKED", "HELD"]);

/** The genuinely in-flight states Ã¢â‚¬â€ a close() call landing here performs no write and only
 * repeats the idempotent launch. */
const IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES: ReadonlySet<TenantLifecycleStatus> = new Set(["DELETING", "QUIESCING", "PURGING"]);

export interface CloseOrganizationResult {
  tenantId: string;
  status: TenantLifecycleStatus;
  /** False when the record was already DELETING+ and this call only repeated the launch. */
  transitioned: boolean;
}

export class CloseOrganizationService {
  constructor(
    private readonly store: SystemMutationStore,
    private readonly reader: TenantLifecycleReader,
    private readonly executions: TenantPurgeExecutionStarter,
    private readonly tableName: string,
    private readonly now: () => string = () => new Date().toISOString(),
  ) {}

  async close(ctx: RequestContext): Promise<CloseOrganizationResult> {
    const tenantId = ctx.tenant.tenantId;
    authorize({ context: ctx, action: "organization:close", resource: { tenantId } });

    const record = await this.reader.read(tenantId);
    if (!record) {
      throw new NotFoundError("Organization lifecycle record not found.", { organizationId: tenantId });
    }
    if (CLOSURE_UNAVAILABLE_STATUSES.has(record.status)) {
      throw new OrganizationClosureUnavailableError(undefined, { organizationId: tenantId, status: record.status });
    }

    let transitioned = false;
    if (record.status === "ACTIVE") {
      try {
        await transitionTenantLifecycle({
          store: this.store,
          tableName: this.tableName,
          tenantId,
          from: "ACTIVE",
          to: "DELETING",
          expectedVersion: record.version,
          now: this.now,
        });
        transitioned = true;
      } catch (err) {
        if (!(err instanceof SystemMutationConflictError)) throw err;
        // A concurrent close() (double-click, retried request) won the race. Re-read once: if the
        // record legitimately landed on an in-flight state, this call simply joins that closure
        // and proceeds to the shared idempotent launch below. Anything else Ã¢â‚¬â€ still ACTIVE, or
        // raced into a stuck state Ã¢â‚¬â€ is genuinely unexpected and is not papered over.
        const after = await this.reader.read(tenantId);
        if (!after || !IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES.has(after.status)) throw err;
      }
    } else if (!IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES.has(record.status)) {
      // Exhaustiveness guard: ACTIVE, the 4 unavailable states, and the 3 in-flight states cover
      // every TenantLifecycleStatus. Reaching here means a status was added without deciding what
      // closing should do with it Ã¢â‚¬â€ fail loudly rather than silently launching an execution.
      throw new OrganizationClosureUnavailableError(undefined, { organizationId: tenantId, status: record.status });
    }

    await this.executions.startExecution({ name: tenantId, input: { tenantId } });

    return { tenantId, status: transitioned ? "DELETING" : record.status, transitioned };
  }
}

  "organization:update-settings": OWNER_ROLES,

};

export type AuthorizationDenialReason = "TENANT_MISMATCH" | "NO_MEMBERSHIP" | "INSUFFICIENT_ROLE" | "RESOURCE_OWNERSHIP_MISMATCH";

export class AuthorizationDeniedError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly reason: AuthorizationDenialReason,
    readonly action: Action,
  ) {
    super(`Authorization denied for action "${action}": ${reason}`);
    this.name = "AuthorizationDeniedError";
  }
}

/**
 * authorize() Ã¢â‚¬â€ implementation-blueprint.md Ã‚Â§4.3: "authorize() verifica primeiro
 * igualdade de tenant, depois papel e vÃƒÂ­nculo por recurso." Throws
 * AuthorizationDeniedError (never returns false) so callers cannot forget to check
 * a boolean result Ã¢â‚¬â€ the http layer maps this to AuthorizationError (403).
 *
 * Order matters and is deliberately fail-closed at every step:
 *  1. context must carry at least one role (no membership => no access at all).
 *  2. if a resource is supplied, resource.tenantId MUST equal context.tenant.tenantId Ã¢â‚¬â€
 *     this is the check that makes cross-tenant ID substitution fail, independent of
 *     role, and independent of what the caller *claims* the resource's tenant is (the
 *     resource object here must always be populated from a DB read keyed by the
 *     authenticated tenantId, never from client input Ã¢â‚¬â€ see repository contract).
 *  3. role must be sufficient for the action.
 *  4. if the resource declares an owner/assignee, membership role alone isn't enough
 *     for actions that are resource-scoped by ownership in the future; MVP has no
 *     per-item ownership finer than tenant, so this step is a no-op today but kept
 *     explicit so a future item-level ACL doesn't require re-deriving this function.
 */
export function authorize(input: AuthorizationInput): void {
  const { context, action, resource } = input;
  const roles = context.tenant.roles as Role[];

  if (roles.length === 0) {
    throw new AuthorizationDeniedError("NO_MEMBERSHIP", action);
  }

  if (resource && resource.tenantId !== context.tenant.tenantId) {
    throw new AuthorizationDeniedError("TENANT_MISMATCH", action);
  }

  const allowedRoles = ACTION_ROLES[action];
  const hasRole = roles.some((role) => allowedRoles.has(role));
  if (!hasRole) {
    throw new AuthorizationDeniedError("INSUFFICIENT_ROLE", action);
  }

  if (resource?.assigneeUserId && resource.ownerUserId) {
    const isOwnerOrAssignee =
      resource.ownerUserId === context.principal.userId ||
      resource.assigneeUserId === context.principal.userId;
    // OWNER and ADMIN bypass per-resource ownership (tenant-wide content admin, B2B-7 -
    // ADMIN has parity with OWNER over business resources, see authorization.ts role model
    // comment above), MEMBER/VIEWER scoped resources require ownership match once per-item
    // ACLs exist. This is enforced only when both fields ARE present (defensive for future
    // use), never invented from nothing.
    if (!roles.includes("OWNER") && !roles.includes("ADMIN") && !isOwnerOrAssignee) {
      throw new AuthorizationDeniedError("RESOURCE_OWNERSHIP_MISMATCH", action);
    }
  }
}

/**
 * resolveRequestContext Ã¢â‚¬â€ Multi-User B2B, docs/architecture/multi-user-b2b-physical-model.md
 * Ã‚Â§11. Steps:
 *  1. validation already performed by the API Gateway authorizer (JWT signature/exp) Ã¢â‚¬â€ this
 *     function receives already-validated claims, it does not verify JWT signatures;
 *  2. bootstrap the global identity (`IdentityBootstrapService`, 2-item atomic create) Ã¢â‚¬â€
 *     authentication no longer creates any tenant/Organization;
 *  3. classify onboarding state (`OnboardingStateResolver`, Wave B2B-4/D-094) Ã¢â‚¬â€ only
 *     `HAS_USABLE_MEMBERSHIP` proceeds to a working `RequestContext`, everything else throws
 *     `OnboardingRequiredError` carrying the exact state;

 *     Wave B2B-6/D-101) when present, else the (today) single `ACTIVE` Membership; both paths

 *  6. build the immutable RequestContext.

import { AuthenticationError, InternalError, OnboardingRequiredError, OrganizationSelectionRequiredError, OrganizationUnavailableError, UnsupportedMembershipRoleError } from "../../../shared/errors/app-error.js";
import { UserRepository } from "../persistence/user-repository.js";
import { GlobalUserRepository } from "../persistence/global-user-repository.js";
import { IdentityBootstrapService } from "./bootstrap-identity.js";
import { OnboardingStateResolver } from "../../organization/application/onboarding-state.js";

/** Claims already validated (signature + expiry) by the API Gateway JWT authorizer. */
export interface ValidatedClaims {
  sub: string;
  tokenId: string; // jti
  issuedAt: string; // iat, ISO-8601
  expiresAt: string; // exp, ISO-8601
  deviceId?: string;
}

export interface ResolveRequestContextInput {
  claims: ValidatedClaims;
  requestId: string;
  correlationId: string;
  /** From `X-Organization-Id` (BFF-derived, Wave B2B-6/D-101) Ã¢â‚¬â€ REQUIRED (not `?:`), even
   * though `undefined` is a valid value, so the compiler blocks every real call site (56 across
   * 13 HTTP handler files, `grep -rl` verified) from silently forgetting to thread it through. */
  organizationIdHint: string | undefined;
}

export interface IdGenerator {
  newUserId(): string;
  newSessionId(): string;
}

export class RequestContextResolver {
  private readonly bootstrap: IdentityBootstrapService;
  private readonly onboarding: OnboardingStateResolver;

  constructor(
    private readonly users: UserRepository,
    private readonly globalUsers: GlobalUserRepository,
    private readonly organizations: OrganizationStore,
    private readonly ids: IdGenerator,
    store: IdentityStore,
    tableName: string,
  ) {
    this.bootstrap = new IdentityBootstrapService(store, tableName);
    this.onboarding = new OnboardingStateResolver(organizations);
  }

  async resolve(input: ResolveRequestContextInput): Promise<RequestContext> {
    const { claims } = input;

    const newUserId = this.ids.newUserId();
    const { user } = await this.bootstrap.bootstrapUser(claims.sub, newUserId);

    if (user.identityStatus !== "ACTIVE") {
      throw new AuthenticationError("User is not active.", { userId: user.userId });
    }

    // Step 5 (user-global watermark, Ã‚Â§10 Ã¢â‚¬â€ was UserProfile.globalLogoutAfter pre-cutover).
    if (user.globalLogoutAfter && claims.issuedAt < user.globalLogoutAfter) {
      throw new AuthenticationError("Session revoked (global logout).", { userId: user.userId });
    }

    let deviceSession;
    if (claims.deviceId) {
      deviceSession = await this.globalUsers.getDeviceSession(user.userId, claims.deviceId);
      if (deviceSession) {
        if (deviceSession.status === "REVOKED") {
          throw new AuthenticationError("Session revoked (device logout).", { deviceId: claims.deviceId });
        }
        if (deviceSession.deviceLogoutAfter && claims.issuedAt < deviceSession.deviceLogoutAfter) {
          throw new AuthenticationError("Session revoked (device logout).", { deviceId: claims.deviceId });
        }
      }
    }
    const sessionId = deviceSession?.sessionId ?? this.ids.newSessionId();

    const onboardingState = await this.onboarding.resolve(user.userId);
    if (onboardingState !== "HAS_USABLE_MEMBERSHIP") {
      throw new OnboardingRequiredError(onboardingState, { userId: user.userId });
    }

    const membership = await this.resolveActiveMembership(user.userId, input.organizationIdHint);

    const roles = this.resolveRoles(membership.role);

    // ProfileService's invariant ("a UserProfile is guaranteed to already exist by the time any
    // RequestContext resolves") must keep holding post-cutover, now per-Organization instead of
    // per-legacy-tenant Ã¢â‚¬â€ provisioned lazily here, the first time this (organizationId, userId)
    // pair resolves, instead of at bootstrap time (no Organization is known yet at bootstrap).
    await this.users.createProfileIfAbsent({
      tenantId: membership.organizationId,
      userId: user.userId,
      identitySubject: claims.sub,
      emailNormalized: user.emailNormalized,
      roles,
      status: "ACTIVE",
    });

    return {
      requestId: input.requestId,
      correlationId: input.correlationId,
      principal: {
        userId: user.userId,
        cognitoSubject: claims.sub,
        sessionId,
        deviceId: claims.deviceId,
      },
      tenant: {
        tenantId: membership.organizationId,
        membershipId: membership.membershipId,
        roles,
      },
      auth: {
        issuedAt: claims.issuedAt,
        expiresAt: claims.expiresAt,
        tokenId: claims.tokenId,
      },
    };
  }

  /**
   * Physical model Ã‚Â§11's resolution chain: `... -> BFF session.activeOrganizationId (seleÃƒÂ§ÃƒÂ£o)
   * -> GetItem direto Membership(userId, organizationId) -> TenantLifecycleRecord ACTIVE ->
   * RequestContext`. Wave B2B-6 (D-101) closes the transport gap D-095 left open (achado 2.1) -
   * `organizationIdHint` (from `X-Organization-Id`, BFF-derived, never client-controlled) is
   * revalidated via `resolveWorkingOrganization()` (consolidates Membership ACTIVE + lifecycle
   * ACTIVE - replaces the separate `AuthenticationError` this function used to throw for the
   * lifecycle half of that check). Hint absent falls back to deriving via GSI4: exactly one
   * ACTIVE Membership (today's common case, unchanged behavior) or a named, non-crashing error
   * for 0/>1 - no writer produced a 2nd ACTIVE Membership for the same user before Wave B2B-8
   * made it reachable, per D-095/D-096's own registered deviation.
   */
  private async resolveActiveMembership(userId: string, organizationIdHint: string | undefined): Promise<Membership> {
    if (organizationIdHint) {
      const result = await resolveWorkingOrganization(this.organizations, userId, organizationIdHint);
      if (result.status === "UNAVAILABLE") {
        throw new OrganizationUnavailableError("This organization is not available in your current context.", { organizationId: organizationIdHint });
      }
      return result.membership;
    }

    const active = await resolveActiveMemberships(this.organizations, userId);
    if (active.length === 0) {
      throw new InternalError("OnboardingStateResolver reported HAS_USABLE_MEMBERSHIP but no ACTIVE Membership was found on re-resolution.", { userId });
    }
    if (active.length > 1) {
      throw new OrganizationSelectionRequiredError("Multiple organizations are available; select one via X-Organization-Id.", { userId, activeCount: active.length });
    }
    const [membership] = active;
    if (!membership) {
      throw new InternalError("Unreachable: active.length === 1 but active[0] is undefined.", { userId });
    }
    // Sem hint, a ÃƒÂºnica Membership ACTIVE ainda precisa da mesma checagem de lifecycle - nunca
    // um atalho que confie na hidrataÃƒÂ§ÃƒÂ£o de resolveActiveMemberships() sozinha (essa funÃƒÂ§ÃƒÂ£o sÃƒÂ³
    // checa Membership.status, nÃƒÂ£o TenantLifecycleRecord).
    const result = await resolveWorkingOrganization(this.organizations, userId, membership.organizationId);
    if (result.status === "UNAVAILABLE") {
      throw new OrganizationUnavailableError("This organization is not available in your current context.", { organizationId: membership.organizationId });
    }
    return result.membership;
  }

  /** B2B-7 (D-097/D-098) closed the gap named in D-095: `authorization.ts` now recognizes all
   * 4 real `Membership.role` values. The assert stays (fail-closed, Codex Rodada 1 achado
   * 2.2/Rodada 2 mudanÃƒÂ§a F, D-095) for any value outside that domain Ã¢â‚¬â€ loud, not silent,
   * instead of letting an unrecognized role fail every `authorize()` check via that matrix's
   * own unsafe cast. */
  private resolveRoles(role: Membership["role"]): string[] {
    if (role !== "OWNER" && role !== "ADMIN" && role !== "MEMBER" && role !== "VIEWER") {
      throw new UnsupportedMembershipRoleError(role);
    }
    return [role];
  }

66:  async close(ctx: RequestContext): Promise<CloseOrganizationResult> {
67:    const tenantId = ctx.tenant.tenantId;
68:    authorize({ context: ctx, action: "organization:close", resource: { tenantId } });
69:
70:    const record = await this.reader.read(tenantId);
71:    if (!record) {
72:      throw new NotFoundError("Organization lifecycle record not found.", { organizationId: tenantId });
73:    }
74:    if (CLOSURE_UNAVAILABLE_STATUSES.has(record.status)) {
75:      throw new OrganizationClosureUnavailableError(undefined, { organizationId: tenantId, status: record.status });
76:    }
77:
78:    let transitioned = false;
79:    if (record.status === "ACTIVE") {
80:      try {
81:        await transitionTenantLifecycle({
82:          store: this.store,
83:          tableName: this.tableName,
84:          tenantId,
85:          from: "ACTIVE",
86:          to: "DELETING",
87:          expectedVersion: record.version,
88:          now: this.now,
89:        });
90:        transitioned = true;
91:      } catch (err) {
92:        if (!(err instanceof SystemMutationConflictError)) throw err;
93:        // A concurrent close() (double-click, retried request) won the race. Re-read once: if the
94:        // record legitimately landed on an in-flight state, this call simply joins that closure
95:        // and proceeds to the shared idempotent launch below. Anything else Ã¢â‚¬â€ still ACTIVE, or
96:        // raced into a stuck state Ã¢â‚¬â€ is genuinely unexpected and is not papered over.
97:        const after = await this.reader.read(tenantId);
98:        if (!after || !IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES.has(after.status)) throw err;
99:      }
100:    } else if (!IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES.has(record.status)) {
101:      // Exhaustiveness guard: ACTIVE, the 4 unavailable states, and the 3 in-flight states cover
102:      // every TenantLifecycleStatus. Reaching here means a status was added without deciding what
103:      // closing should do with it Ã¢â‚¬â€ fail loudly rather than silently launching an execution.
104:      throw new OrganizationClosureUnavailableError(undefined, { organizationId: tenantId, status: record.status });
105:    }
106:
107:    await this.executions.startExecution({ name: tenantId, input: { tenantId } });
108:
109:    return { tenantId, status: transitioned ? "DELETING" : record.status, transitioned };
110:  }
111:}

20:import type { EntityKey } from "../dynamodb/occ.js";
21:
22:/**
23: * Forward-only state machine (approved design Ã‚Â§G):
24: *   ACTIVE -> DELETING -> QUIESCING -> PURGING -> VERIFIED -> DELETED
25: * Any of DELETING/QUIESCING/PURGING/VERIFIED can additionally move to BLOCKED/HELD (stuck
26: * state Ã¢â‚¬â€ legal hold or a purge error that keeps failing) and back to the SAME state once
27: * remediated. ACTIVE is never re-entered from any other state (no "un-delete") and DELETED
28: * is a true terminal Ã¢â‚¬â€ nothing transitions out of it (the sweeper described in the design
29: * doc repairs residue in place, it never re-opens the lifecycle record's status).
30: */
31:export type TenantLifecycleStatus =
32:  | "ACTIVE"
33:  | "DELETING"
34:  | "QUIESCING"
35:  | "PURGING"
36:  | "VERIFIED"
37:  | "DELETED"
38:  | "BLOCKED"
39:  | "HELD";
40:
41:export interface TenantLifecycleRecord extends EntityKey {
42:  SK: "LIFECYCLE";
43:  entityType: "TenantLifecycleRecord";
44:  tenantId: string;
45:  status: TenantLifecycleStatus;
46:  /** Set when entering BLOCKED/HELD and cleared on remediation back to the prior state Ã¢â‚¬â€ a
47:   * short machine-readable reason for the stuck state (e.g. "PURGE_S3_ERRORS",
48:   * "LEGAL_HOLD"), never free text containing tenant PII. */
49:  blockedReason?: string;
50:  /** The state BLOCKED/HELD was entered from, so remediation knows where to resume Ã¢â‚¬â€
51:   * required whenever status is BLOCKED/HELD, absent otherwise. */
52:  blockedFrom?: TenantLifecycleStatus;
53:  createdAt: string;
54:  updatedAt: string;
55:  version: number;
56:}
57:
58:export function tenantLifecycleKey(tenantId: string): EntityKey {
59:  return { PK: `TENANT#${tenantId}#LIFECYCLE`, SK: "LIFECYCLE" };
60:}
61:
62:/**
63: * Statuses under which a `TenantBusinessMutation` may be admitted Ã¢â‚¬â€ deliberately just
64: * `ACTIVE` (approved design Ã‚Â§H invariant 1: "Nenhuma mutaÃƒÂ§ÃƒÂ£o de negÃƒÂ³cio tenant-scoped
65: * commita em DynamoDB sem ConditionCheck de TenantLifecycleRecord.status = ACTIVE").
66: */
67:export const TENANT_ACTIVE_STATUS: TenantLifecycleStatus = "ACTIVE";
68:
69:/** Forward-only transition graph. A state maps to the set of states it may legally move to
70: * next; BLOCKED/HELD's own allowed targets depend on `blockedFrom` (checked separately by
71: * `canResumeFromBlocked`, since the graph itself can't express "return to wherever you came
72: * from" as a fixed edge list). */
73:const FORWARD_TRANSITIONS: Record<TenantLifecycleStatus, ReadonlySet<TenantLifecycleStatus>> = {
74:  ACTIVE: new Set(["DELETING"]),
75:  DELETING: new Set(["QUIESCING", "BLOCKED", "HELD"]),
76:  QUIESCING: new Set(["PURGING", "BLOCKED", "HELD"]),
77:  PURGING: new Set(["VERIFIED", "BLOCKED", "HELD"]),
78:  VERIFIED: new Set(["DELETED", "BLOCKED", "HELD"]),
79:  DELETED: new Set([]),
80:  BLOCKED: new Set([]), // only canResumeFromBlocked() below, not a fixed forward edge
81:  HELD: new Set([]),
82:};
83:
84:/**
85: * True if `from -> to` is a legal forward transition, OR a remediation resume out of
86: * BLOCKED/HELD back to the exact state it was blocked from. Never true for anything that
87: * would re-enter ACTIVE or leave DELETED Ã¢â‚¬â€ those two guarantees are the entire point of
88: * this fence (approved design Ã‚Â§H invariant 4, Ã‚Â§Q "no ACTIVE reversion, no DELETED
89: * resurrection").
90: */
91:export function canTransition(from: TenantLifecycleStatus, to: TenantLifecycleStatus, blockedFrom?: TenantLifecycleStatus): boolean {
92:  if (to === "ACTIVE") return false; // never re-enter ACTIVE from anywhere
93:  if (from === "DELETED") return false; // DELETED is terminal, nothing leaves it
94:  if ((from === "BLOCKED" || from === "HELD") && blockedFrom) {
95:    return to === blockedFrom;
96:  }
97:  return FORWARD_TRANSITIONS[from]?.has(to) ?? false;
98:}
99:
100:export class InvalidTenantLifecycleTransitionError extends Error {
101:  constructor(
102:    public readonly from: TenantLifecycleStatus,
103:    public readonly to: TenantLifecycleStatus,
104:  ) {
105:    super(`Invalid TenantLifecycleRecord transition: ${from} -> ${to}`);
106:    this.name = "InvalidTenantLifecycleTransitionError";
107:  }
108:}
109:
110:/** Throws InvalidTenantLifecycleTransitionError instead of returning false Ã¢â‚¬â€ for callers
111: * (e.g. the future lifecycle-transition worker) that want a fail-fast assertion rather than
112: * a boolean they must remember to check. */
113:export function assertValidTransition(from: TenantLifecycleStatus, to: TenantLifecycleStatus, blockedFrom?: TenantLifecycleStatus): void {
114:  if (!canTransition(from, to, blockedFrom)) {
115:    throw new InvalidTenantLifecycleTransitionError(from, to);
116:  }
117:}

# Quarantine/Recovery Window + LGPD Retention Gaps Ã¢â‚¬â€ Round 3 (Claude proposal, reconciliation)

Round 2 scored 7.3/10 Ã¢â‚¬â€ real progress (5.5Ã¢â€ â€™7.3) but Codex correctly flagged the `executionArn`
persistence race as still-open, the RBAC/no-RequestContext contradiction, missing legal-hold
interaction, retry idempotency (new UUID per retry vs. per attempt), an ASL modeling error, and a
LGPD backlog with real omissions/an incorrect semantic claim. Fixing all of these, not just the
labeled ones.

## Fix 1 Ã¢â‚¬â€ `executionArn` persistence race (Codex's "most important remaining gap")

Solved by removing the race entirely, not by hardening the write: **Step Functions execution ARNs
are deterministic** Ã¢â‚¬â€ `arn:aws:states:{region}:{account}:execution:{stateMachineName}:{executionName}`.
Since `executionName = ${tenantId}-${closureAttemptId}` is already chosen by the caller BEFORE
`StartExecution` runs (fix 3 below fixes when it's chosen), the ARN needs no read-back and no
separate persistence step Ã¢â‚¬â€ the cancellation path (and the composition root generally) computes it
from `(stateMachineArn, tenantId, closureAttemptId)`, all of which are already persisted on
`TenantLifecycleRecord` at the moment `HELD_FOR_RECOVERY` is written, in the SAME
`TransactWriteItems` as the status transition. No `executionArn` field needed at all Ã¢â‚¬â€ it is a pure
function of already-persisted data, so it is removed from the persisted schema (was a real
complexity Codex correctly flagged; the right fix is deleting it, not defending it).

## Fix 2 Ã¢â‚¬â€ Retry idempotency: `closureAttemptId` generated once per attempt, not per call

`closureAttemptId` is generated **only** on the `ACTIVE Ã¢â€ â€™ HELD_FOR_RECOVERY` transition itself (one
UUID, written in that transaction). Every subsequent call to `close()` while already
`HELD_FOR_RECOVERY` (retry, double-click) reads the EXISTING `closureAttemptId`/`recoveryDeadline`
off the record and reuses them for the (idempotent, name-derived) `StartExecution` call Ã¢â‚¬â€ never
generates a new one. This is the same idiom `close-organization.ts` already uses for the
`ACTIVE`-only branch (`transitioned=false` path calling the shared launch with the existing name) Ã¢â‚¬â€
extended, not invented. Execution name length: `tenantId` in this system is `org_${ulid()}` (`src/runtime/aws/ids.ts`,
`newOrganizationId`) = 4 + 26 = 30 chars; `closureAttemptId` as a UUID v4 = 36 chars; concatenated
with a `-` separator = 67 chars, inside Step Functions' 80-character execution name limit Ã¢â‚¬â€
verified against the actual ID format, not assumed (Round 2 cited a nonexistent `src/shared/ids.ts`
and asserted "16-64 chars" without checking; corrected here after actually reading the real file).

## Fix 3 Ã¢â‚¬â€ Dedicated authorization primitive for the no-RequestContext cancel path

Codex is right that `organization:cancel-close` in `ACTION_ROLES` is dead code if the cancel path
never builds a `RequestContext` to call `authorize()` with. Fix: **no generic `Action` union entry**
Ã¢â‚¬â€ the cancel path uses a new, narrow, dedicated function
`authorizeCancelClosure(membership: Membership): void` (co-located with `authorization.ts`, not
inside it) that throws the SAME `AuthorizationDeniedError` type and emits the SAME
`security-audit.ts` denial-event shape (`action: "organization:cancel-close"` as a literal string
tag in the event payload, not a member of the `Action` union Ã¢â‚¬â€ the taxonomy in `security-audit.ts`
already accepts arbitrary action strings for audit purposes, only `authorize()`'s `ACTION_ROLES`
matrix requires the union) if `membership.role !== "OWNER" || membership.status !== "ACTIVE"`. This
is named explicitly as a deliberate, audited exception to the normal `authorize()` path Ã¢â‚¬â€ not a
second RBAC system Ã¢â‚¬â€ because the entire premise of this cancel path is operating on a tenant that
cannot resolve a normal `RequestContext` in the first place.

## Fix 4 Ã¢â‚¬â€ Legal hold / `BLOCKED` interaction during the quarantine window

Named explicitly (was silently absent in Round 2): `HELD_FOR_RECOVERY Ã¢â€ â€™ BLOCKED` is added as a
legal transition (`blockedFrom: "HELD_FOR_RECOVERY"`), triggered the same way `DELETING`&co. already
enter `BLOCKED` today (operator action / a purge-adjacent error Ã¢â‚¬â€ during quarantine specifically,
this is realistically only a manual legal hold, since no purge work runs yet). Remediation from
`BLOCKED` returns to `blockedFrom` (existing pattern, unchanged) Ã¢â‚¬â€ i.e., back to
`HELD_FOR_RECOVERY`, resuming the SAME `recoveryDeadline`/`closureAttemptId` (not restarting the
clock; a legal hold pauses enforcement, it does not reset the countdown, consistent with
`privacy-lgpd.md` Ã‚Â§3's "hold suspends purge, never cancels it permanently without review").
Cancellation is unavailable while `BLOCKED` (already covered by
`CLOSURE_UNAVAILABLE_STATUSES` unchanged from Round 1/2).

**Metadata retention on cancel**: `recoveryDeadline`/`closureAttemptId` are never cleared on
`HELD_FOR_RECOVERY Ã¢â€ â€™ ACTIVE` Ã¢â‚¬â€ retained on the record as an audit trail of the last closure attempt
(read-only once the status moves off `HELD_FOR_RECOVERY`); the NEXT close() attempt overwrites them
with a fresh value on the next `ACTIVE Ã¢â€ â€™ HELD_FOR_RECOVERY` transition. No separate cleanup step.

## Fix 5 Ã¢â‚¬â€ ASL modeling error: `Choice` cannot read DynamoDB

Codex is correct Ã¢â‚¬â€ a `Choice` state evaluates its own input, it cannot query DynamoDB. Corrected
shape: `Wait(30d) Ã¢â€ â€™ Task(ReadTenantLifecycleRecord, ConsistentRead) Ã¢â€ â€™ Choice(status ==
"HELD_FOR_RECOVERY"?) Ã¢â€ â€™ [true: Task(TransitionToDeleting) Ã¢â€ â€™ existing Wait(1800s)+purge chain] /
[false: Succeed("cancelled-or-already-progressed")]`. One new Lambda (`ReadTenantLifecycleRecord`,
thin wrapper over the same reader interface `CloseOrganizationService` already uses) Ã¢â‚¬â€ named
explicitly as new infra surface for the future implementation session, not glossed over as "just a
Choice".

## Fix 6 Ã¢â‚¬â€ LGPD backlog: correcting the real omissions

Codex found real gaps, accepted without argument:

- **`USER_DOCUMENT`/`EXTRACTION_TRANSIENT`/`InvitationTokenPointer` (TRANSIENT)** were omitted from
  the backlog because they already have real physical purge (W3-06, M7 lifecycle, `invitation-
  token.ts`) Ã¢â‚¬â€ should have been listed explicitly as **"already implemented, zero backlog work"**
  rather than silently absent (a reader diffing this list against `privacy-lgpd.md`'s 9 classes
  would reasonably read the omission as an oversight, not a decision).
- **`CORE_USER_DATA`** scope corrected to match the matrix definition exactly ("itens, polÃƒÂ­ticas,
  ocorrÃƒÂªncias" Ã¢â‚¬â€ `privacy-lgpd.md` line 38): includes policies, not just items/occurrences.
- **Semantic error corrected**: the matrix's event for `CORE_USER_DATA` is "exclusÃƒÂ£o/encerramento",
  not "vencimento" Ã¢â‚¬â€ an item's due date passing is NOT a deletion trigger (items past due stay
  fully live in this product, that's the entire point of an expiration tracker). The real gap is:
  when a user/service **explicitly deletes** an `ExpirationItem` (soft-delete already exists per
  the domain model), nothing purges the underlying record 30 days later. Backlog item #1 restated
  correctly: worker that scans soft-deleted `ExpirationItem`/policy records past `deletedAt + 30d`.

**Corrected executable-lane backlog** (same 6 slots, semantics fixed):
1. `CORE_USER_DATA` Ã¢â‚¬â€ soft-deleted `ExpirationItem`/policy records, `deletedAt + 30d` (corrected
   trigger event).
2. `DELIVERY_RECORD` Ã¢â‚¬â€ `createdAt + 180d`, unchanged from Round 2.
3. `SECURITY_AUDIT` Ã¢â‚¬â€ `createdAt + 365d`, unchanged.
4. `QUOTA_TELEMETRY` Ã¢â‚¬â€ window-end + 30d, unchanged.
5. `ACCOUNT_ACTIVE` (non-closure case) Ã¢â‚¬â€ `Invitation` expired/revoked, then removed `Membership`,
   then `Channel` (unchanged ordering, still the most ambiguous sub-case).
6. `TRANSIENT` remainder (`WebhookInbox`, `UploadSlot`) Ã¢â‚¬â€ unchanged, lowest exposure.

**Already done, explicitly not backlog** (the correction itself): `USER_DOCUMENT`,
`EXTRACTION_TRANSIENT`, `InvitationTokenPointer`/`TRANSIENT`'s token-pointer slice.

**Blocked lane** (unchanged from Round 2): `LEGAL_EVIDENCE`, gated on legal approval + independent
KMS + Object Lock, not part of the linear order.

# Quarantine/Recovery Window + LGPD Retention Gaps — Round 5 (Claude proposal, reconciliation)

Round 4 scored 8.7/10. 4 items remain (1 partial + 1 new + 1 not-fixed + 1 Round-3 leftover). All
closed here.

## Fix 1 — Durable reconciliation for `HELD_FOR_RECOVERY` after `StopExecution` succeeds but the OCC restore keeps failing

The single retry in Round 4 was not durable. Fix: the SAME sweeper Lambda that already runs daily
post-`DELETED` (`tenant-purge-sweeper`, D-124) gains a second responsibility — reconcile
`HELD_FOR_RECOVERY` records where `recoveryDeadline` has passed AND a cancellation was attempted
(a new boolean flag, `cancellationRequested`, set by `CancelOrganizationClosureService` in the SAME
transaction as the first restore attempt, before calling `StopExecution` — durable evidence a
cancel was in flight even if the rest of the operation never completes). For each such record: call
`DescribeExecution` on the deterministic ARN; if the execution is confirmed
`ABORTED`/`SUCCEEDED`/nonexistent (i.e., genuinely not running), retry
`transitionTenantLifecycle(HELD_FOR_RECOVERY → ACTIVE, expectedVersion)` — same idempotent-repair
idiom the sweeper already uses for `DELETED` residue, just applied to a different terminal
condition. This closes the gap without inventing a new mechanism: the daily sweeper cadence is the
existing durable retry loop, not a new one. `cancellationRequested` gives the sweeper a way to find
these records without a table scan for `HELD_FOR_RECOVERY` alone (same GSI query shape the sweeper
already uses).

## Fix 2 — `security-audit.ts` contract corrected; new error given a real shape

The contract is `{ reason: string; action: string }`, `action` deliberately typed `string`
(confirmed by re-reading the file, not asserted) — so `"organization:cancel-close"` logs
correctly, no change needed there beyond describing it accurately. `ClosureCancellationDeniedError`
is specified concretely: extends `AppError`, `category: "AUTHORIZATION"`, `code:
"CLOSURE_CANCELLATION_DENIED"`, `retryable: false` — same shape every other `AppError` subclass in
`app-error.ts` already follows, not a hand-wave.

## Fix 3 — `ReminderOccurrence` (not the nonexistent `RecurrenceOccurrence`), real async cascade named honestly

Correcting the factual error: the entity is `ReminderOccurrence`
(`reminder-materializer.ts`), and `ExpirationService.deleteItem()` does NOT atomically purge it —
it emits `expiration.item-deactivated.v1`, and `ReminderMaterializer.cancelAllOccurrences()`
cancels (status change) occurrences asynchronously in response — cancellation, not physical
deletion. **This means `CORE_USER_DATA`'s backlog item #1 was actually two workers, not one**:
1. `ExpirationItem`/policy soft-deleted records past `deletedAt + 30d` — physical purge worker
   (as Round 3 described, now correctly scoped to just these two entities).
2. `ReminderOccurrence` records left `CANCELLED` by the existing event-driven flow above — a
   SEPARATE physical purge worker, triggered off the same `deletedAt + 30d` signal read from the
   parent item (occurrences don't carry their own `deletedAt`; the purge worker for these joins
   against the parent's status, same join the reminder flow itself already performs to find them).

Named as 2 backlog units instead of 1 — the priority order itself is unchanged (still slot #1
overall), only the internal decomposition is corrected.

## Fix 4 — Identity resolution for the cancel path, closing Round 3's still-open item

`CancelOrganizationClosureService`'s entry point resolves `cognitoSub → userId` via a direct
`IdentityMapping` lookup (`identity-mapping-repository.ts`, already used read-only elsewhere in this
codebase for exactly this kind of lookup, e.g. by `resolve-request-context.ts` itself before it
goes on to the parts of resolution this cancel path deliberately skips) — **read-only, never
triggers `bootstrapUser()`/onboarding**: if no `IdentityMapping` exists for the `cognitoSub`, the
cancel request fails with `NotFoundError` (the user has never completed login/bootstrap at all,
which cannot be true for anyone who could have triggered the original `close()` — `close()` itself
requires a resolved `RequestContext`). This is the one explicit deviation from normal resolution:
skip `RequestContextResolver`'s Organization-membership/lifecycle-status gating (the entire reason
this dedicated path exists) while still reusing its identity primitive, not reinventing identity
lookup.

## Estado final

codex
Round 4 improves the design, but it still does not clear 9.0.

1. `StopExecution` succeeds, OCC restoration fails — PARTIALLY FIXED.

The reread correctly distinguishes legitimate lifecycle progress from a transient conflict. However, retrying the transition only once does not provide complete compensation. If that retry also conflicts or fails transiently, the tenant remains `HELD_FOR_RECOVERY` with its execution permanently stopped. “Fail loudly” provides observability, not recovery.

The design needs a durable reconciliation path or an explicitly retryable operation that eventually restores `ACTIVE` when the same `closureAttemptId` remains current.

2. Legal hold modeled as `HELD` — FIXED.

`HELD_FOR_RECOVERY → HELD`, with `blockedFrom: HELD_FOR_RECOVERY`, now matches the lifecycle model’s distinction between legal holds and operational failures. The post-deadline release behavior is also explicitly decided.

3. `authorizeCancelClosure` type contract — FIXED, with a NEW problem.

A dedicated `ClosureCancellationDeniedError` avoids passing `"organization:cancel-close"` into the `Action`-typed `AuthorizationDeniedError`, and keeping audit logging at the HTTP boundary preserves the existing purity boundary.

New problem: the proposal inaccurately says `security-audit.ts` has free-form `reason`/`context` fields. Its actual contract is:

```ts
{ reason: string; action: string }
```

The design can log `action: "organization:cancel-close"` because that field is deliberately typed as `string`, but it must describe that real contract. The new error should also explicitly extend `AppError` with category `AUTHORIZATION`, a stable code, and `retryable: false`, rather than merely saying it belongs to the same “family.”

4. `RecurrenceOccurrence` in the `CORE_USER_DATA` backlog — NOT FIXED.

There is no `RecurrenceOccurrence` entity in the codebase; the actual entity is `ReminderOccurrence`. More importantly, `ExpirationService.deleteItem()` does not atomically delete occurrences. It emits `expiration.item-deactivated.v1`, after which the reminder materialization flow cancels occurrences asynchronously. Cancellation is not physical deletion and does not establish the claimed 30-day retention purge.

Therefore the backlog must explicitly name `ReminderOccurrence` and define its physical-purge mechanism and trigger. The asserted existing atomic cascade is false.

Additional unresolved issue: Round 3 also identified that cancellation must resolve authenticated `cognitoSub` through `IdentityMapping` without bootstrap/onboarding before authorization. Round 4 does not close that contract.

Weighted score:

- Duração fundamentada: 22/25
- Mecanismo cross-cutting: 17/20
- Cancelamento real: 18/20
- Priorização LGPD: 12/15
- Preservação das decisões aprovadas: 9/10
- Escopo de implementação: 9/10

Total: 87/100.

I do not believe both graders should clear 9.0 yet. The remaining cancellation-reconciliation gap and the incorrect occurrence-purge claim are substantive, not editorial.
